items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: Les Gatie was my first teacher. He showed me how to hold the sticks

ctx.x: I mean before you were twelve it was just —

I started playing at five. My mother was a pianist. She played the hell out of “Shine on Harvest Moon,” I remember that. And she was a musician. She was a piano player in a silent movie house where my father used to sit there and do a whole bunch of movies, and fell in love with her and they got married and that kind of stuff. And there was always music in my house. We had a piano. During the depression my dad wasn’t working very much, and we always had a piano, and I assumed, doesn’t everybody — in the middle of…
You practiced? What a unique idea.
